modern: From Plato: The man who has a lofty mind and takes a view of all time and of all substance, do you suppose it possible for him to think that human life is anything great? It is not possible, he said.—Such a man, then, will think that death also is no evil.—Certainly not.

explained.summary:
Marcus copies a passage from Plato’s Republic: a person with a large mind who takes in all of time and all of existence can’t think a single human life is anything great, and so won’t think death is anything bad.

He quotes it because it captures a favourite exercise of his own: zooming out to the scale of the cosmos so that his own life and death shrink to their true proportions.
